description: Everything this image tracks is a version pinned in a comment-annotated line, so it is all custom regex managers. Two of them matter most: the Spilo base (a new base means new Postgres minors and security fixes) and the Supabase refs (a new ref means new bootstrap SQL, which CI then forces into the same PR).

dockerfile.description: Off deliberately. The base image arrives through ARG interpolation in FROM, and Renovate resolves the ARG default -- so the built-in manager finds ghcr.io/zalando/spilo-18 once per build stage, on top of the custom manager below, and the same bump would be proposed three times. The custom manager wins because it carries versioning=regex for Spilo's 4.1-pN scheme, which plain docker versioning would mis-order against 4.10-p1.

customManagers.description: Dockerfile ARGs. Renovate's dockerfile manager cannot read the base image here because the tag arrives through ARG interpolation in FROM, so the ARG lines are annotated instead.
The Supabase release ref in upstream.env, which decides which bootstrap SQL gets vendored.
The supabase/supabase commit the self-host-only SQL is vendored from. That path has no release of its own, so it is tracked as a branch digest.

packageRules.description: supabase/postgres tags include build artefacts (-amchecktest, -orioledb-*, -x86) and at least one malformed entry with an 8-digit final component (17.6.1.15799999). The regex versioning drops the suffixed ones; this caps the final component to keep the malformed ones out.
The Spilo base and the Supabase SQL are the two bumps that change behaviour rather than just patch levels - keep them in their own PRs so the diff is reviewable.
Statically linked into pg_net.so, so it gets no distro security updates - these should land promptly.
